source.title: Dynamic adaptive threshold based learning for noisy annotations robust facial expression recognition
source.authors: Darshan Gera; B. Rajkumar; Naveen Siva Kumar Badveeti; S. Balasubramanian

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or garbling affects the relevant results.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how synthetic label corruption affects facial-expression classification, using test accuracy and training curves rather than the original studies’ random-label memorization setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracies under 10%, 20%, and 30% synthetic label corruption and describes training/test curves at 30%. It does not test completely random labels, unstructured inputs, training-time cost, explicit regularization, or learning order. Cited claims about networks fitting clean data before noisy labels are prior work, not this study’s result.
record.test_reason: The standard cross-entropy ResNet-18 baseline tests the test-error component of V4 in facial-expression recognition: accuracy decreases monotonically at 10%, 20% and 30% random label corruption on all three datasets. Perfect training fit is not established. The proposed noise-robust method's performance does not independently test the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that dynamic class-specific clean-sample selection and consistency training mitigate noisy-label overfitting and yield effective FER performance on synthetic and real noisy datasets.
record.recipe_differences: Uses ResNet-18 with a dynamic class-specific sample threshold, warm-up, weak and strong augmentation, and supervised plus consistency losses; the baseline is ResNet-18 trained with cross-entropy. The paper studies partially corrupted FER labels, not completely random labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance is reported at different corruption fractions and datasets. The paper also studies loss-weight and warm-up choices, but those ablation figures do not test the claim versions directly.

fits_no_version.finding: DNFER improves held-out performance while reducing training accuracy relative to the baseline through sample selection and consistency training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selecting reliable labels and applying consistency training can mitigate overfitting under partially corrupted facial-expression labels.

record.problems: Training-curve values are only in figures and described qualitatively in text; the text does not state that baseline training accuracy reaches zero error. The experiments use 10–30% synthetic label noise, not fully random labels. The proposed DNFER changes the training procedure. Table 1 reports accuracy but not training-set error.
record.rows_left_out: None. Table 1 values for the baseline, DNFER, and named comparators are retained for RAFDB, FERPlus, and AffectNet-8 at 10%, 20%, and 30% noise; the training-curve findings described in Section 4.4.4 are retained for all three datasets.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, zero or near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Time to fit random versus true labels and convergence slowdown across corruption fractions.
Perfect training fit across corruption levels, corruption above 30%, and approach to chance at complete randomization. Saturating training curves do not establish zero error.
Necessity and sufficiency of weight decay, dropout and augmentation, including generalization after their removal.
Separate learning trajectories for real and corrupted labels. The learning-order statements cite prior work; aggregate training/test curves do not isolate those trajectories.

missing.what: Baseline held-out accuracy at 0% added corruption on RAFDB and FERPlus, needed to extend the within-model corruption comparison to its uncorrupted endpoint. These are plotted but their values are unavailable in the supplied text.

record.verdict_notes: The record's limits_scope verdicts are unwarranted: unreported perfect training fit is an untested component, and variation over training epochs is not variation over corruption fraction. DNFER deliberately changes training to resist memorization. Implementation uses a face-recognition-pretrained ResNet-18 with Adam; the supplied document is a 2022 preprint associated with the study identifier.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labels, zero or near-zero training error, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training time to fit true versus random labels and convergence versus corruption fraction.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.

The reported table gives test accuracy at 10–30% corruption, but does not report training-set fit across corruption fractions; training curves are described only for 30% corruption. Exact curve values are figure-only.
Weight decay, dropout, data augmentation as regularizers, and generalization after removing them.
Whether this study’s models learn real-label patterns before memorizing noisy or random labels.

relationships.condition: Test-error component only: standard cross-entropy ResNet-18 baseline, 10–30% symmetric label corruption on RAFDB, FERPlus and AffectNet-8.
relationships.reason: Accuracy declines monotonically: RAFDB 81.74→79.60→74.31 (R1/R7/R13), FERPlus 85.87→84.02→82.30 (R19/R23/R27), and AffectNet-8 57.21→56.23→52.60 (R31/R37/R43); perfect training fit is unverified.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy declined successively from 81.74 to 79.60 to 74.31 on RAFDB, 85.87 to 84.02 to 82.30 on FERPlus, and 57.21 to 56.23 to 52.60 on AffectNet-8.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Baseline ResNet-18 under 30% synthetic label noise on RAFDB, FERPlus, and AffectNet-8
reader_labels.reason: Baseline training accuracy is said to saturate, but the text does not say it reaches perfect fit; test accuracy initially rises and then drops rather than being described as steadily worsening with noise fraction (R49, R51, R53). The test-accuracy table shows deterioration as noise rises on RAFDB, while the table alone does not measure training fit (R1, R7, R13).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: DNFER under 10–30% synthetic label noise on RAFDB, FERPlus, and AffectNet-8
reader_labels.reason: Test accuracies are reported across corruption levels, but the training curves show lower training accuracy than Baseline and the method changes the training procedure; the study does not establish perfect training fit with the standard recipe (R6, R12, R18, R22, R26, R30, R36, R42, R48, R50, R52, R54).
